title: Lawson-Haggart concerts and Dick Gibson's World's Greatest Jazz Band
summary: Leeman describes concert tours with Lawson and Haggart, and how Gibson formed the World's Greatest Jazz Band from their arrangements, with Morey Feld on drums when Leeman was ill.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Now, as we progress with the albums, Haggard wished to increase the personnel on the records for some of the arrangements that he was doing. They wanted us to -- I've been associated with Bob Haggard and Yank Lawson, and the Lawson-Haggard Band. Since then, and those were the early boys, up until now -- up until the present time. Up until the last few years, I've been doing concerts -- they've done concerts all over the world, and I've done a great deal of them with them. Once in awhile, I would be busy on other projects, and they'd use other drummers. They've done that twice in Europe because I was busy with my Switzerland

International Jazz Concert in Bern.
However, we've kept the mutual admiration society alive, and we're still open for concerts. I do tours, I've done several this past year, and the reason we're not doing concerts now probably is because Bob Haggart has bought a home in Mexico, and that late in the Fall, he goes to Mexico to his home, which leaves the Lawson-Haggart band hanging. We don't want to do any concerts without Hag.
And then I'm expecting any time now, this is February -- in another month or so, Haggart will be coming back from Mexico, trotting back, as it may be -- and the Mexican Foxtrot is implied there, and we will be doing more this year -- concerts, that is.
There was a while in the late sixties, Richard Gibson decided to form a band and he took Bob Haggart and Yank Lawson, and used their arrangements, and that was the nucleus of what he found was the World's Greatest Jazz Band. At the time they formed, I was ill, and the now departed, and great drummer, Morey Feld, was used -- and he, once he was in the World's Greatest Jazz Band, we've all gotten to dislike that name -- the world's 'greatest' -- it reminds me of Mrs. Astor on the Titanic, when it struck the iceberg, and she said, "I rang for ice, but this is ridiculous!"
However, that's pertaining to the title, 'the world's greatest'. They were close! And in that period until they

broke up, until they broke away from Richard Gibson, he sold the band to an agent in Arizona, and his name -- he still is the bassist for the World's Greatest Jazz Band, of Yank Lawson and Bob Haggard. His name is Bark Hickox, and anybody who'd ever like to hear the World's Greatest Jazz Band in person -- we're open for engagements. His address is 4350 East Camelback Road, Phoenix, Arizona 85108.
